A second-cycle course (**3MB00A**, 7.5 ECTS, Umeå University) on the mathematical
and statistical methods that underpin modern bioinformatics. The emphasis is on application
rather than abstract mathematics.

## Where to start

- [**Course plan**](courseplan.md) — the official syllabus: outcomes, examination, entry requirements.
- [**Learning outcomes**](elo.md) — what we are trying to teach, day by day.

## Before you start

- [**Install R and the packages you need**](intro/install.qmd) — do this before you start the first unit.

## Topics

The course runs over five weeks. Work through the sidebar from top to bottom:

- **Week 1: Linear systems, vectors, transformations** — solving systems by hand and in R, vectors and projection, matrices as transformations of points and images; applications in flow-cytometry compensation and polar coordinates.
- **Week 2: Bases, eigenvectors, PCA, Markov chains** — eigenvalues, Markov chains and their stationary distribution, principal component analysis, and the Fourier basis.
- **Week 3: Linear models & differential expression** — least squares, design matrices for age, sex, BMI, batch and time, confounding and Simpson's paradox, differential expression with limma, bulk RNA-seq with DESeq2 (counts, size factors).
- **Week 4: Penalized models & Bayesian statistics** — an overview: ridge, lasso and cross-validation; Bayesian vs. frequentist, Bayesian regression, count error models (Poisson, negative binomial), hierarchical models, and penalties as priors.
- **Week 5: Nonlinear models & latent spaces** — beyond linear models, nonlinear embeddings (UMAP) and variational autoencoders, with single-cell RNA-seq as the application.
- **Candidate material** (optional) — Material not included in this course round. But if you have time left over, feel free to browse it! Covers R-STAN, worked Bayesian and penalized cases, cell cycle, single-cell QC in depth (doublets, mitochondrial and ribosomal reads), image filters, continuous-time and hidden Markov models, OPLS, chemometrics and multiome integration.

Each unit lists its lecture, quiz and exercises in teaching order. **See Canvas for the most up to date study instructions and bonus hand-in material**.
